requirements: Reproduce the DUET disaggregated hybrid Mamba-Transformer accelerator, including its configurable systolic and vector-unit array microarchitectures, the full-stack simulator, design-space exploration, and the reported performance/power/area results across three models and four workloads.

sub_tasks.requirements: Set up the RTL synthesis, SRAM modeling, DRAM timing, and technology-scaling toolchain used to characterize DUET's hardware.
Establish the RTL implementation and synthesis flow for the FP16 systolic and vector-unit arrays in TSMC 28 nm.
Code has been implemented that provides SystemVerilog RTL sources for the FP16 systolic array and the FP16 W-wide vector-unit array microarchitectures.

verification.spec: Check that the repository contains SystemVerilog (.sv or .v) source files implementing (a) the configurable FP16 systolic array and (b) the FP16 W-wide vector-unit array. Verify by finding files with module declarations for a systolic array (containing rows/cols parameters and MAC PEs) and a vector-unit array (containing vector width W parameter). Both must synthesize cleanly with a standard tool (e.g., Verilator or yosys front-end parse).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that configures Synopsys Design Compiler with the TSMC 28 nm standard-cell library and drives synthesis of the systolic and vector-unit array RTL to produce area, power, and timing reports.

verification.spec: Check that the repository contains a Synopsys Design Compiler script (.tcl) configuring the TSMC 28 nm standard-cell library (link_library/target_library) and driving synthesis of both systolic and vector-unit array RTL. Script must produce area, power, and timing reports. Verify by parsing the tcl for read_verilog/analyze commands, compile/compile_ultra, and report_area/report_power/report_timing commands.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that parameterizes the RTL/synthesis flow so that the 64x32 systolic array and the 32-wide 16x8 vector-unit array configurations selected by DSE can each be synthesized in TSMC 28 nm.

verification.spec: Verify the RTL/synthesis flow accepts parameters for array dimensions and vector width. Elaborate/synthesize (or dry-run synth scripts) both configurations: 64x32 systolic array and 32-wide 16x8 vector-unit array in TSMC 28 nm (or open-source equivalent PDK if TSMC 28nm unavailable, documenting the substitution). Confirm both configurations pass elaboration and generate synthesis reports.

sub_tasks.requirements: The synthesis flow reports FP16 datapath at 16-bit precision consistent with the paper's assumption that 16-bit is the predominant data format for LLMs.

verification.spec: Inspect the systolic array and vector-unit array RTL source and verify all datapath signals (operand registers, MAC inputs/outputs, accumulators, and I/O ports) are declared with 16-bit width, consistent with FP16 precision. Also check any parameter DATA_WIDTH or similar defaults to 16.

sub_tasks.requirements: The synthesis of the 64x32 systolic array in TSMC 28 nm reports a maximum operating frequency of 763 MHz.

verification.spec: Synthesize the 64x32 FP16 systolic array RTL using Synopsys Design Compiler with the TSMC 28 nm standard-cell library. Perform timing analysis to determine the maximum operating frequency (Fmax) from the synthesis timing report. Verify Fmax is 763 MHz within tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The synthesis of the 32-wide 16x8 vector-unit array in TSMC 28 nm reports a maximum operating frequency of 763 MHz.

verification.spec: Synthesize the 32-wide 16x8 FP16 vector-unit array RTL using Synopsys Design Compiler with the TSMC 28 nm standard-cell library. Extract Fmax from the timing report. Verify Fmax is 763 MHz within tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Integrate CACTI 7.0 to model on-chip SRAM buffer area, power, and access energy at the bandwidths used by the Prefill and Decode chiplets.

Code has been implemented that invokes CACTI 7.0 with configuration files parameterizing SRAM size, technology node (32 nm), and target bandwidth to produce area/energy estimates for the local buffers.

verification.spec: Run the CACTI 7.0 invocation script(s) with configuration files specifying (a) 1 MB SRAM at 256 GB/s in 32 nm (systolic local buffer) and (b) 1 MB SRAM at 1024 GB/s in 32 nm (vector-unit local buffer). Confirm CACTI produces area/energy outputs and that reported areas are within 20% of paper values (4.51 mm^2 and 6.55 mm^2 respectively).

sub_tasks.requirements: The CACTI-based SRAM model for the systolic-array chiplet buffer (1 MB, 256 GB/s) reports an area of 4.51 mm^2 in 32 nm.

verification.spec: Run CACTI 7.0 with a 1 MB SRAM configuration providing 256 GB/s bandwidth at 32 nm technology node. Extract the reported area. Verify the area is approximately 4.51 mm^2.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CACTI-based SRAM model for the vector-unit-array chiplet buffer (1 MB, 1024 GB/s) reports an area of 6.55 mm^2 in 32 nm.

verification.spec: Run CACTI 7.0 with a 1 MB SRAM configuration providing 1024 GB/s bandwidth at 32 nm technology node. Extract the reported area. Verify the area is approximately 6.55 mm^2.

sub_tasks.requirements: Integrate DRAM timing modeling via Ramulator to produce cycle-accurate memory traces consumed by the simulator.
Code has been implemented that runs Ramulator (2.0) to generate DRAM timing traces for the GDDR7 and HBM3e memory configurations used in the Prefill and Decode packages.

verification.spec: Execute the Ramulator 2.0 invocation script that generates DRAM timing traces for both GDDR7 (24 stacks, 128 GB/s each) and HBM3e (12 stacks, 1 TB/s each) configurations. Verify each run completes and produces trace files consumable by the DUET simulator.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented providing Ramulator configuration files for GDDR7 (128 GB/s per stack, 8 GB per stack) and HBM3e (1 TB/s per stack) matching the DUET package memory specifications.

verification.spec: Locate Ramulator configuration files in the repo. Parse them and assert: GDDR7 config declares 128 GB/s per stack and 8 GB per stack capacity; HBM3e config declares 1 TB/s per stack. Confirm both files are referenced by simulator config.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that ingests Ramulator-generated timing traces into the DUET simulator so that DRAM latencies are consumed by the event-driven memory/NoI model.

verification.spec: Feed a Ramulator-generated trace into the DUET simulator's memory model and issue a batch of memory requests. Verify that DRAM latencies observed by the event-driven memory/NoI model match the trace's per-request timing (spot-check >=50 requests). Confirm no fallback to a hardcoded latency.

sub_tasks.requirements: Integrate the FlexSFU-based SFU model and D2D/UCIe PHY area models needed to compute chiplet footprints.
Code has been implemented that models SFU area using FlexSFU (28 nm) parameters, producing 0.95 mm^2 for 64 SFUs (systolic chiplet) and 3.8 mm^2 for 256 SFUs (vector-unit chiplet).

verification.spec: Locate the SFU area model in code/config. Assert per-SFU 28nm area from FlexSFU is applied and total SFU area equals 0.95 mm^2 for 64 SFUs in the systolic chiplet and 3.8 mm^2 for 256 SFUs in the vector-unit chiplet (within 5% rounding).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that models each 8-lane, 25 Gbps GRS-style D2D PHY as 0.3876 mm^2 in 16 nm and applies UCIe x64 advanced-package microbump area assumptions when computing chiplet area budgets.

verification.spec: Inspect the D2D PHY area model. Verify each 8-lane 25 Gbps GRS PHY contributes 0.3876 mm^2 in 16 nm. Verify Prefill chiplet uses 11 PHYs and Decode chiplet uses 42 PHYs. Confirm UCIe x64 advanced-package microbump area is included in the chiplet area budget calculation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Set up the DeepScale-based technology-scaling flow to project 28 nm/32 nm/16 nm components to 7 nm chiplet area budgets.
Code has been implemented that uses DeepScale scaling factors to translate the 28 nm compute-array, 32 nm SRAM, and 16 nm D2D PHY area/power numbers into 7 nm equivalents.

verification.spec: Run the area-scaling code path with 28nm compute arrays, 32nm SRAM, and 16nm D2D PHY inputs. Verify DeepScale scaling factors are applied to each component (checking intermediate values), producing 7 nm equivalent areas. Confirm the summed chiplet area (with 40% overhead margin) fits within 121 mm^2 for both Prefill and Decode chiplets.

sub_tasks.requirements: The chiplet-area computation reserves an additional 40% area on top of the summed component areas to account for controllers, routing, and physical-design overhead when projecting to 7 nm.

verification.spec: Inspect the 7 nm chiplet area-computation code. Verify that after summing all component areas (systolic/vector arrays, SRAM, SFU, D2D PHYs, microbumps) scaled to 7 nm, a 40% additional overhead factor (i.e., multiplication by 1.40 or division by 0.60) is applied for controllers, routing, and physical-design overhead.

sub_tasks.requirements: The 7 nm chiplet-area budgeting enforces a per-chiplet cap of 121 mm^2, matching the HBM footprint for floorplanning consistency, and a total package interposer area limit in the 2700-3000 mm^2 range.

verification.spec: Inspect the chiplet/package area-budgeting script or config. Verify: (a) per-chiplet area cap is set to 121 mm^2, (b) the total interposer area budget is enforced within the 2700-3000 mm^2 range. Confirm both DUET Prefill (16 compute chiplets + 12 memory-PHY chiplets) and DUET Decode (8 compute chiplets + 12 HBM stacks) configurations satisfy these limits.

sub_tasks.requirements: Reproduce the in-house full-stack LLM cycle-accurate simulator that integrates systolic/vector-unit compute models, event-driven NoI, and Ramulator-based DRAM traces, matching the public DUET repository.
Simulator repository scaffolding and top-level driver expose configurable systolic/vector-unit arrays and can run an LLM inference trace end-to-end.
Code has been implemented that clones/reproduces the DUET simulator layout from github.com/AlishKanani/DUET, exposing entry points for prefill (systolic) and decode (vector-unit) simulation modes.

verification.spec: Clone the DUET repository (github.com/AlishKanani/DUET). Verify presence of top-level directories/scripts for both prefill (systolic-array) and decode (vector-unit) simulation modes, and that entry-point scripts (e.g., run_prefill.py, run_decode.py or equivalents) exist and are importable / executable with --help.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented providing a top-level simulator driver that accepts an LLM model description, workload trace, and hardware configuration file and produces per-phase cycle counts and event logs.

verification.spec: Invoke the top-level simulator driver with a sample model description (e.g., a small Mamba-Transformer), a workload trace, and a hardware config JSON/YAML. Confirm it runs to completion and emits per-phase (prefill/decode) cycle counts and event logs to disk.

sub_tasks.requirements: Configuration files parameterize chiplet counts, systolic array dimensions (rows x cols), vector-unit width W and array size, SRAM bandwidth, and DRAM type (GDDR7 vs HBM3e), and are consumed by the simulator without code changes.

verification.spec: Take a base hardware config file and produce 3-4 variants that change (a) chiplet count, (b) systolic array rows/cols, (c) vector-unit W and array size, (d) SRAM bandwidth, (e) DRAM type (GDDR7 vs HBM3e). Run the simulator on each variant with NO code changes. Confirm all runs succeed and that reported peak compute/bandwidth in the log reflect the changed parameters.

sub_tasks.requirements: Cycle-accurate compute models for systolic array and vector-unit array with RTL-validated behavior for GEMM, GEMV, and SSM kernels.

Code has been implemented that models the configurable systolic-array PE pipeline cycle-by-cycle, including the two SSM-specific registers, three-cycle SSM micro-pipeline, and mode-bit switch between SSM (state-stationary) and GEMM (output-stationary) dataflows.

verification.spec: Run a unit test that instantiates the PE model, then: (1) set mode-bit to SSM, drive a state-stationary SSM step and verify the two SSM-specific registers are updated per the three-cycle micro-pipeline (mul for B_k*u_bar_k, A_bar_k*X_k, then C_k*X_k), and X_k is held locally across steps; (2) set mode-bit to GEMM, drive an output-stationary GEMM and verify the SSM registers are clock-gated (unchanged) while partial sums accumulate in the output register.

sub_tasks.requirements: The systolic-array simulator sustains one SSM update every three cycles after an O(N) pipeline fill for the state-stationary dataflow, verified on a synthetic SSM trace.

verification.spec: Run the systolic-array simulator on a synthetic SSM kernel with state dimension N and sequence length L. Record cycle at which the first output token is produced (pipeline fill = O(N)) and cycles between successive output tokens in steady state. Assert the steady-state throughput is 1 SSM update per 3 cycles (i.e., token k+1 completes 3 cycles after token k for k >> N).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that models the W-wide vector-unit array cycle-accurately, including three vector registers per VU, MAC + tree reduction with O(log N) latency, and scalar MAC chain for N>W state slices.

verification.spec: Run a unit test that instantiates the vector-unit array model with configurable W and array dimensions. Verify: (1) each VU exposes 3 vector registers (R1, R2, R3), (2) dot-product across a W-wide vector completes in O(log W) cycles via a tree-reduction schedule, (3) when N > W, the simulator recruits N/W VUs in the same column and combines partial CX results via a scalar MAC chain (one MAC per VU). Assert results match a numpy reference and cycle counts scale as documented.

sub_tasks.requirements: The vector-unit simulator produces identical output token values to a golden Python reference for both GEMV and SSM-decode kernels on a suite of unit tests.

verification.spec: Run a suite of unit tests: (a) GEMV: random FP16 matrix W of shape [M, K] and vector x of shape [K]; simulate on the vector-unit array; compare output y against numpy y = W @ x with FP16 rounding tolerance. (b) SSM-decode single-token: given A_bar, B, C, D, X_{k-1}, u_k, simulate one decode step; compare X_k and y_k against a golden Python reference implementation of Equation 1. Both suites must pass (max abs error < FP16 ULP-based bound).

sub_tasks.requirements: The simulator's per-kernel cycle counts have been validated against the SystemVerilog RTL implementation of the 64x32 systolic array and 32-wide 16x8 vector-unit array with cycle-level agreement (deviation reported and within the paper's stated validation).

verification.spec: For a representative set of kernels (GEMM tile, GEMV, single-step SSM decode, long-sequence SSM prefill), run both the cycle-accurate Python/C++ simulator and an RTL simulation (Verilator/VCS) of the 64x32 systolic and 32-wide 16x8 vector-unit arrays. Record per-kernel cycle counts from both. Assert per-kernel cycle-count deviation between simulator and RTL is within the stated validation margin (e.g., <=5%), matching the paper's claim of cycle-accurate validation against RTL.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that models the SFU column (systolic side) and SFU row (vector side) executing exp, SiLU, and other non-linear ops in-situ without SRAM write-back, feeding results directly into the PE/VU pipeline.

verification.spec: Trigger a compute step that requires an SFU non-linear op (e.g., exp for A_bar computation or SiLU) in both the systolic (SFU column) and vector-unit (SFU row) paths. Instrument SRAM to record writes. Assert SFU output feeds directly into PE/VU pipeline registers with NO intermediate SRAM write-back. Verify numeric output matches numpy reference for exp/SiLU within FP16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Event-driven Network-on-Interposer and D2D PHY model for chiplet-to-chiplet and chiplet-to-memory communication.

Code has been implemented that provides an event-driven NoI simulator tracking per-chiplet request/response queues and per-link occupancy with configurable topology (4x4 for Prefill, 4x5 with interleaved HBM columns for Decode).

verification.spec: Instantiate the event-driven NoI with (a) 4x4 topology (Prefill package) and (b) 4x5 topology with interleaved HBM columns (Decode package) from config. Inject a synthetic all-to-all traffic pattern. Verify per-chiplet queue depths and per-link occupancy counters advance over time and are readable via the simulator's stats API.

sub_tasks.requirements: D2D PHY bandwidths are parameterized to 256 GB/s for Prefill chiplets and 1024 GB/s for Decode chiplets and enforced as link-bandwidth caps in the event-driven simulator.

verification.spec: Set Prefill D2D link bandwidth to 256 GB/s and Decode D2D to 1024 GB/s in config. Inject a saturating traffic stream on a D2D link and measure sustained bytes/cycle in the simulator. Confirm sustained BW does not exceed configured caps (within 1%) and that reducing the config value proportionally reduces measured BW.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that models inter-package cache transfer (KV cache and SSM state) over NVLink/UALink-like off-package links and overlaps this transfer with next-layer compute during LLM inference.

verification.spec: Run a small multi-layer LLM inference where after each layer's prefill, the KV/state cache is transferred over an NVLink/UALink-modeled off-package link to the Decode package. Verify from the simulator's event trace that the transfer for layer L overlaps in time with compute for layer L+1 on the Prefill package (transfer start_time < next-layer compute end_time).

sub_tasks.requirements: The NoI model correctly serializes conflicting requests on shared links and reports link utilization statistics per simulation run.

verification.spec: Inject two concurrent flows targeting the same NoI link. Verify from event trace that requests are serialized (non-overlapping link occupancy windows) and that the final stats dump includes per-link utilization percentages summing consistently with injected traffic.

sub_tasks.requirements: DRAM timing model driven by Ramulator 2.0 traces for both GDDR7 (Prefill) and HBM3e (Decode) memory subsystems.
Code has been implemented that generates or consumes Ramulator 2.0 timing traces to model DRAM latency and bandwidth for memory accesses issued by the simulator.

verification.spec: Confirm the simulator can consume a pre-generated Ramulator 2.0 timing trace file: run with the trace and verify that DRAM request completions in the simulator log match trace-reported latencies for a sampled set of >=50 requests.

sub_tasks.requirements: GDDR7 configuration in the DRAM model provides 128 GB/s per stack and 24 stacks total for the Prefill package, yielding 3 TB/s aggregate bandwidth and 192 GB capacity.

verification.spec: Inspect the DRAM/memory configuration file for the Prefill package. Verify: per-stack bandwidth is set to 128 GB/s, number of GDDR7 stacks is 24, per-stack capacity is 8 GB, resulting in aggregate 3 TB/s bandwidth and 192 GB total capacity.

sub_tasks.requirements: HBM3e configuration in the DRAM model provides 1 TB/s per stack and 12 stacks for the Decode package, yielding 12 TB/s aggregate bandwidth and 288 GB capacity.

verification.spec: Inspect the DRAM/memory configuration file for the Decode package. Verify: per-stack bandwidth is set to 1 TB/s, number of HBM3e stacks is 12, resulting in aggregate 12 TB/s bandwidth and 288 GB total capacity.

sub_tasks.requirements: The DRAM model reports sustained bandwidth measurements that match the configured peak within a documented tolerance under a streaming read benchmark trace.

verification.spec: Run a streaming-read benchmark trace against the HBM3e-configured DRAM model (12 stacks x 1 TB/s = 12 TB/s peak). Measure sustained BW reported by the simulator over a long window. Verify sustained BW is within 15% of the 12 TB/s peak configured.

sub_tasks.requirements: Full-stack integration that composes compute, NoI, and DRAM models into a unified LLM inference simulation loop.

Code has been implemented that enforces KV/state cache capacity limits per package and correctly refuses or partitions batch sizes that exceed capacity (reproducing e.g. the B200/prefill-friendly inability to run batch>64 on ArXiv with Nemotron-H-56B).

verification.spec: Configure the simulator to run Nemotron-H-56B on ArXiv with the B200 baseline at batch sizes 32, 64, 80, 128. Assert the simulator refuses/skips or explicitly flags B>64 as infeasible due to KV/state cache capacity, while DUET completes all batches. Also test that manually overriding cache capacity to a small value causes even the DUET config to refuse.

sub_tasks.requirements: Prepare Nemotron-H-56B, Zamba2-7B, and Llama3-8B along with ArXiv-4K, BWB, LongWriter-6K, and LMSYS-Chat-1M workloads at the batch-size sweep used in the paper.
Acquire and configure the three LLM architectures used in the paper (Nemotron-H-56B, Zamba2-7B, Llama3-8B), extracting the per-layer structural parameters needed by the simulator.

Code has been implemented to obtain the Nemotron-H-56B hybrid Mamba-Transformer model configuration (layer counts, Mamba-to-attention ratio, hidden/embedding dimension ED, SSM state dimension N) as described in the paper's roofline and workload sections.

verification.spec: Import the model-config loader and load the Nemotron-H-56B config. Assert the returned spec contains fields for total layer count, Mamba layer count, attention layer count, embedding dimension (ED), and SSM state dimension (N). Assert total parameter budget is approximately 56B (within +/-10%).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to obtain the Zamba2-7B hybrid model configuration (Mamba block count, attention block count, ED, N, FFN dimensions) so it can be simulated on DUET and the baselines.

verification.spec: Load the Zamba2-7B model spec. Assert presence of Mamba block count, attention block count, ED, N, and FFN dim fields. Assert parameter count approximately 7B (+/-15%).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to obtain the Llama3-8B pure Transformer model configuration (layer count, heads, KV heads, hidden dimension, FFN size) for use as the Transformer-only evaluation model.

verification.spec: Load the Llama3-8B model spec. Assert presence of layer count, attention heads, KV heads, hidden dim, FFN size. Assert no Mamba/SSM layers are present (pure Transformer). Assert parameter count approximately 8B (+/-15%).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to store each model in a machine-readable spec (e.g., JSON/YAML) enumerating per-layer type (Mamba SSM, attention, FFN) and shape parameters that the simulator consumes to produce GEMM/GEMV/SSM kernel traces.

verification.spec: Load each of the three model specs from their JSON/YAML file. Assert the file parses cleanly, contains a per-layer list where each entry has a 'type' field in {mamba_ssm, attention, ffn} (or equivalent), and shape parameters. Feed one spec into the simulator's kernel-trace generator and assert it produces a nonempty sequence of GEMM/GEMV/SSM kernels.

sub_tasks.requirements: Model specs behave such that Nemotron-H-56B contains a Mamba-to-attention block ratio in the 3:1-7:1 range (Mamba-dominant) consistent with the paper's description of hybrid models.

verification.spec: Load Nemotron-H-56B spec, count Mamba and attention blocks. Assert ratio = mamba_count / attention_count is between 3.0 and 7.0 inclusive.

sub_tasks.requirements: Acquire and preprocess the four workload datasets (ArXiv-4K, BWB, LongWriter-6K, LMSYS-Chat-1M) into prompt-length / decode-length distributions used to drive prefill and decode simulation.
Code has been implemented to download/load the ArXiv long-document dataset [Cohan et al. 2018] and produce the ArXiv-4K workload characterized as long prefill / short decode.

verification.spec: Run the ArXiv-4K workload loader; assert it returns a nonempty list of prompt/decode-length pairs. Verify average prompt length is around 4K tokens (>= 2000) and that decode lengths are relatively short (mean < 1000), matching long-prefill/short-decode profile.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the Bilingual Web Books (BWB) dataset and produce the BWB workload characterized as long prefill / long decode.

verification.spec: Run the BWB workload loader; assert nonempty output, average prompt length long (>= 2000 tokens) and average decode length long (>= 1000 tokens), matching long-prefill/long-decode.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the LongWriter-6K dataset and produce the LongWriter workload characterized as short prefill / long decode.

verification.spec: Run the LongWriter-6K loader; assert nonempty output; average prompt length short (< 2000 tokens) and average decode length long (>= 2000 tokens), matching short-prefill/long-decode.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the LMSYS-Chat-1M dataset and produce the Chat workload characterized as short prefill / short decode.

verification.spec: Run the LMSYS-Chat-1M loader; assert nonempty output; average prompt length short (< 1500 tokens) and average decode length short (< 1000 tokens), matching short-prefill/short-decode.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to tokenize each dataset with the appropriate model tokenizer(s) and emit per-request (prompt_length, decode_length) pairs consumed by the simulator's workload driver.

verification.spec: Invoke the tokenization pipeline for each (dataset, model) pair on a small sample. Assert the output is a list of (prompt_length_int, decode_length_int) tuples and that lengths differ across tokenizers for the same raw text (verifying the tokenizer is actually applied). Feed the tuples into the simulator's workload driver and assert acceptance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The workload-preparation code behaves such that ArXiv-4K and BWB produce distributions with substantially longer average prompt lengths than LongWriter-6K and Chat, matching the paper's long-prefill vs. short-prefill categorization.

verification.spec: Compute mean prompt length for ArXiv-4K, BWB, LongWriter-6K, and Chat using the workload prep pipeline. Assert mean(ArXiv) > 2*mean(LongWriter) and mean(BWB) > 2*mean(Chat), confirming long vs. short prefill categorization.

sub_tasks.requirements: The workload-preparation code behaves such that LongWriter-6K and BWB produce distributions with substantially longer average decode lengths than ArXiv-4K and Chat, matching the paper's long-decode categorization.

verification.spec: Compute mean decode length for the four workloads. Assert mean(LongWriter) > 2*mean(ArXiv) and mean(BWB) > 2*mean(Chat), confirming long vs. short decode categorization.

sub_tasks.requirements: Provide a batch-size sweep and continuous-request driver that binds each (model, workload) pair to the batch sizes used in the paper's evaluation.
Code has been implemented to sweep batch sizes B in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128} (powers of two from 1 to 128) for every model x workload combination, as stated in Section 4.4.

verification.spec: Launch the batch-sweep driver for one (model, workload) pair. Assert the emitted result table contains exactly the batch sizes {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128} (or that the driver's default sweep list equals this set).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to feed a continuous stream of user requests (following DistServe/Mooncake-style assumptions) to the Prefill package and pipe generated KV/state caches to the Decode package for decoding, as described in Section 4.4.

verification.spec: Run the simulator with a continuous request stream (N>=100 requests). Inspect execution trace: assert each request enters the Prefill package first, its KV/state cache is then transferred to the Decode package, and decoding on the Decode package begins after (or overlapped with) the prefill of subsequent requests. Verify inter-package cache transfer events appear in the trace.

sub_tasks.requirements: The batch-size driver behaves such that when B > 64 for Nemotron-H-56B on the ArXiv workload, the B200 GPU and prefill-friendly aggregated baselines are flagged as infeasible due to KV/state cache capacity limits, while the DUET configuration is allowed to run.

verification.spec: Configure the driver to run Nemotron-H-56B on ArXiv for batch sizes [64, 128] against three systems: B200, prefill-friendly aggregated, DUET. Assert both B200 and prefill-friendly return an 'infeasible/OOM' status for B=128, while DUET returns valid TTFT/throughput results.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the configurable systolic-array PE with two extra SSM registers, state-stationary SSM dataflow, SFU column, and output-stationary GEMM mode as described for the Prefill package.
Processing Element (PE) microarchitecture: register file, MAC unit, neighbor links, and control logic.
Code has been implemented for a PE module that contains a single FP16 MAC unit and a local register file, exposed as an RTL/simulator component instantiable inside the systolic array.

verification.spec: Import the PE module class/RTL. Assert it exposes a MAC operation on FP16 operands and contains a register file/register set. In a unit test, feed known operand pairs and verify the MAC output matches expected FP16 product+accumulate within FP16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each PE contains four registers total: two standard operand/accumulator registers (as in conventional systolic PEs) plus two additional SSM-specific registers used to hold intermediate SSM values.

verification.spec: Inspect the PE module in the systolic-array RTL/simulator source. Verify the PE declares exactly four register storage elements: two standard operand/accumulator registers (as in a conventional systolic PE such as Gemmini) plus two additional registers designated for SSM intermediate values. Confirm via source inspection (register names/comments) and by counting register-typed signals in the PE module.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for horizontal (W→E) neighbor links and vertical (N→S) neighbor links between PEs that propagate one word per cycle.

verification.spec: Instantiate a small 2x2 PE mesh. Drive a distinct value onto PE[0,0]'s east output and PE[0,0]'s south output on cycle T. Assert PE[0,1] observes the east value on cycle T+1 and PE[1,0] observes the south value on cycle T+1, verifying one-word-per-cycle propagation in both directions.

sub_tasks.requirements: The PE's lightweight control logic accepts mode bits (SSM vs. GEMM) from the array controller and selects the appropriate datapath and register usage without altering operand tiling or addressing.

verification.spec: Instantiate a PE with mode input. Set mode=SSM and run a canned SSM update micro-sequence; verify the SSM-specific registers are used and results match expected SSM output. Then set mode=GEMM with identical operand tiling and addressing (no configuration change beyond mode bit); verify GEMM MAC output matches expected. Assert operand address sequence is identical between the two runs.

sub_tasks.requirements: In GEMM mode, the two SSM-specific registers are clock-gated (disabled from toggling) so that they do not contribute dynamic switching activity during matrix-multiplication execution.

verification.spec: In the PE RTL/simulator, run GEMM mode and inspect the clock/enable signal of the two SSM-specific registers. Assert the clock-gate enable is deasserted (or the register write-enable is held low) for the entire GEMM execution. Confirm dynamic switching activity counter for those registers is zero during GEMM.

sub_tasks.requirements: Systolic array assembly, SFU column, and SRAM buffer interface.
Code has been implemented that parameterizes a 2D array of PEs with configurable rows and columns and instantiates the concrete 64×32 configuration used by the Prefill package.

verification.spec: Import the systolic array module and instantiate with (rows=64, cols=32); assert the resulting array reports 64*32 = 2048 PEs. Also instantiate with (rows=8, cols=8) and (rows=128, cols=64); assert PE counts of 64 and 8192 respectively, confirming parameterization.

sub_tasks.requirements: A single column of Special Function Units (SFUs) is placed alongside the systolic array, with one SFU per row (64 SFUs for a 64×32 array), providing configurable non-linear operations such as exp and SiLU.

verification.spec: Instantiate the 64x32 systolic array. Assert it contains exactly 64 SFU instances arranged as one column adjacent to the array, with one SFU per row. Assert each SFU supports at least 'exp' and 'SiLU' non-linear operations via a mode/opcode input.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that SFUs read operands directly from on-chip SRAM buffers and feed their results into the PE pipeline, with no intermediate SRAM write-back on that path.

verification.spec: Drive an SFU with an operand loaded from the on-chip SRAM buffer model and route its output into the adjacent PE's input pipeline. Trace all SRAM write ports during the operation and assert no write to SRAM occurs on the SFU-output path (writes may occur elsewhere, but not for the SFU result being consumed in-situ).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the SRAM buffer interface providing input operands to the array edges at up to 256 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, consistent with the Prefill package's GDDR-backed buffer assumption.

verification.spec: Read the SRAM buffer configuration for the Prefill package systolic array. Assert the configured aggregate SRAM-to-array bandwidth equals 256 GB/s (within +/-5%). Also run a bandwidth stress trace and confirm sustained input bandwidth to the array edges saturates at approximately 256 GB/s.

sub_tasks.requirements: An array-level controller module has been implemented that exposes mode bits to switch the whole array between SSM-prefill and GEMM (output-stationary) dataflows at runtime.

verification.spec: Inspect the systolic array RTL/simulator source in the DUET repo for an array-level controller module exposing mode bits (e.g., a mode/config register or port) that switch the array between SSM-prefill dataflow and GEMM output-stationary dataflow. Verify by importing the module and toggling the mode signal at runtime in a testbench and confirming PE behavior changes accordingly.

sub_tasks.requirements: State-stationary SSM-prefill dataflow on the systolic array.
Code has been implemented for the SSM recurrence following Equation 1: X_k = exp(Δ_k A) X_{k-1} + (Δ_k · B_k) u_k and y_k = C_k × X_k + D · u_k, using the notation of Table 2.

verification.spec: Locate the reference SSM computation in the codebase (Python or the simulator). Run it on random A, B_k, C_k, Delta_k, u_k, D, and initial X_{k-1} for a small ED and N. Verify the produced X_k and y_k exactly match a fresh numpy implementation of X_k = exp(Delta_k*A)*X_{k-1} + (Delta_k*B_k)*u_k and y_k = C_k @ X_k + D*u_k using the variable names of Table 2. Max abs error below FP16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The algebraic reordering (Δ_k · B_k) u_k → (Δ_k · u_k) B_k is applied, so that a scalar–scalar multiplication (Δ_k u_k) is computed once and then multiplied by the vector B_k instead of computing two vector-wide multiplications.

verification.spec: Inspect the SSM implementation and verify that the (Delta_k * B_k) * u_k term is computed as (Delta_k * u_k) * B_k, i.e., a scalar-scalar multiplication of Delta_k and u_k is done first, then the resulting scalar multiplies the vector B_k. Confirm via source inspection AND by counting FLOPs/multiply operations: for state dim N, the reordered form uses 1 scalar mul + N scalar-vector muls, versus 2N vector muls for the naive form. Also verify numerical equivalence to the naive ordering on random inputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The SSM mapping unrolls the embedding dimension (ED) across the array rows and the state dimension (N) across the array columns.

verification.spec: Inspect the SSM-to-systolic-array mapping code. Verify that the mapping assigns the embedding dimension index (ED) to the row index of the array and the state dimension index (N) to the column index. Confirm via variable names/comments and by running a mapping example: for a small SSM (ED=8, N=4) on an 8x4 array, verify that PE[i,j] handles embedding element i and state element j.

sub_tasks.requirements: Operand routing streams B_k and C_k vertically (shared across rows) and streams Ā_k, ū_k, and (Du)_k horizontally (shared across columns), matching the parameter-sharing pattern in Figure 3(b).

verification.spec: Instantiate the systolic array in SSM mode with instrumented operand ports. Drive distinct tagged values for B_k, C_k on the north (vertical) inputs and A_bar_k, u_bar_k, (Du)_k on the west (horizontal) inputs. Trace signals over one SSM step and verify B_k/C_k propagate top-to-bottom shared across rows, while A_bar_k/u_bar_k/(Du)_k propagate left-to-right shared across columns, matching Figure 3(b).

sub_tasks.requirements: Each PE holds exactly one element of the recurrent state X_k locally (state-stationary) across consecutive SSM steps, updating it in place rather than fetching from external SRAM.

verification.spec: Run the simulator on an SSM prefill with sequence length L>=4 and instrument the PE local state register X. For each PE[i,j], record the value of X across L SSM steps and verify: (a) X is updated in place each step using the local A_bar_k*X + B_k*u_bar_k computation, (b) X is never read from external SRAM (i.e., the SRAM read counters for the state variable remain zero after initial load, if any). Assert state-stationary behavior.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each PE implements a three-cycle micro-pipeline performing element-wise multiplication for B_k ū_k, Ā_k X_k, and the partial product C_k X_k using the two extra SSM registers.

verification.spec: Trace one PE through a single SSM step in the cycle-accurate model. Verify that exactly three consecutive cycles are used for element-wise mults: cycle 1 computes B_k*u_bar_k (stored in SSM reg 1), cycle 2 computes A_bar_k*X_k (stored in SSM reg 2, X_k then updated with sum), cycle 3 computes C_k*X_k (partial product). Assert the three-cycle micro-pipeline schedule and that the two additional SSM registers hold these intermediates.

sub_tasks.requirements: Partial sums for computing y_k are forwarded horizontally between PEs and accumulated along the row, while the updated state remains stationary in each PE.

verification.spec: Run the systolic array in SSM-prefill mode over multiple tokens. Trace per-PE state register: assert the state X value remains in the same PE across tokens (state-stationary). Trace horizontal wires along a row: assert partial sums accumulate along the row to yield y_k at the row output while state register values do not shift.

sub_tasks.requirements: All element-wise SSM intermediates (B_k ū_k, Ā_k X_k, and partial C_k X_k terms) are consumed in-place inside the PE pipeline; the simulator/RTL contains no external SRAM write-backs of these intermediates during SSM execution.

verification.spec: Instrument the SRAM interface of the systolic array module. Run an SSM-prefill kernel for several tokens and record all SRAM write transactions. Assert that no SRAM writes correspond to the element-wise intermediates B_k*u_bar_k, A_bar_k*X_k, or partial C_k*X_k terms; only final outputs y_k (and streamed inputs) may touch SRAM.

sub_tasks.requirements: Only SSM input parameters (Ā_k, ū_k, B_k, C_k, (Du)_k) and activations are streamed into the array during SSM execution; the state X_k is never fetched from SRAM in steady state.

verification.spec: Run the systolic array through a multi-token SSM prefill. Monitor SRAM read addresses/tags and array input operands. After the initial O(N) pipeline fill, assert that SRAM reads correspond only to A_bar_k, u_bar_k, B_k, C_k, (Du)_k and activations, never to X_k. Verify X_k lives exclusively in the state register of each PE during steady state.

sub_tasks.requirements: After an initial O(N) pipeline-fill latency, the array sustains one full SSM update every three cycles in steady state.

verification.spec: Run the systolic-array simulator on an SSM kernel with state dimension N (e.g., N=32) and sequence length L >> N (e.g., L=2048). Measure the first-output cycle latency (should be O(N)) and steady-state throughput as (cycles_used_from_token_N_to_L) / (L - N). Assert steady-state throughput equals exactly 3 cycles per SSM update.

sub_tasks.requirements: A functional unit test drives a small SSM example (e.g., ED and N chosen so the workload fits in a 64×32 array) through the state-stationary dataflow and verifies that the produced y_k sequence matches a reference Python/NumPy implementation of Equation 1 bit-exactly (or within FP16 rounding).

verification.spec: Set up a small SSM instance with ED=64, N=32 that fits a 64x32 array. Generate random FP16 inputs (A, B_k, C_k, Delta_k, u_k for k=1..L=8, and D). Run the state-stationary systolic simulator to produce y_k for all k. Independently compute y_k via numpy using Equation 1. Assert y_k matches the numpy reference bit-exactly or within FP16 rounding tolerance (max abs error <= 2^-10 * max_magnitude).

sub_tasks.requirements: Output-stationary GEMM mode on the same systolic array.
Code has been implemented for an output-stationary GEMM dataflow on the same array, where inputs (activations and weights) stream in from the array edges and partial sums accumulate in each PE.

verification.spec: Instantiate the systolic array in GEMM mode. Configure with random FP16 matrices A [M,K] and B [K,N] that tile the array. Simulate the output-stationary dataflow where A streams horizontally from the west edge, B streams vertically from the north edge, and partial sums accumulate in each PE's output register. Verify output C = A @ B matches a numpy reference within FP16 tolerance. Also inspect PE trace to confirm partial sums accumulate locally rather than being forwarded.

sub_tasks.requirements: In GEMM mode, operand tiling, buffering, and addressing (for SRAM and the array edges) are identical to those used in SSM mode; only the mode bits change PE behavior, with no data re-layout required.

verification.spec: Load an operand tile into SRAM and buffers as configured for SSM mode, then switch mode bits to GEMM without touching SRAM contents or buffer addresses. Confirm that the same tiling/addressing sequence produces correct GEMM outputs. Compare SRAM address traces between SSM and GEMM runs for identical operand shapes: only PE mode bits differ, no re-layout stage exists.

sub_tasks.requirements: A functional unit test executes representative GEMM shapes from attention and feed-forward layers on the array in GEMM mode and confirms bit-accurate (or FP16-tolerant) equivalence to a reference matrix-multiplication routine.

verification.spec: Execute representative attention and FFN GEMM shapes (e.g., 64x128x256 tiles typical of Nemotron-H layers) on the 64x32 systolic array in GEMM mode. Compare outputs against numpy/torch FP16 matmul reference and assert max abs error < 1e-2 (FP16 rounding tolerance).

sub_tasks.requirements: In GEMM mode, the per-cycle throughput and utilization of the array match that of a conventional (baseline) output-stationary systolic array of identical dimensions, i.e., there is no measurable performance degradation from adding the SSM-specific registers.

verification.spec: Instantiate the DUET systolic array in GEMM mode and a reference baseline output-stationary systolic array of identical dimensions (64x32). Run a suite of randomized GEMM workloads (e.g., 128x128, 256x256, 512x512 FP16 matmuls) and compare cycle counts and PE utilization. Assert that DUET's cycle count and utilization match the baseline within <=1% (SSM-specific registers must be clock-gated in GEMM mode).

sub_tasks.requirements: RTL cycle-accuracy validation and mode-switching correctness of the configurable systolic array.

The cycle-accurate model of the systolic array in the in-house simulator is validated against the SystemVerilog RTL by comparing cycle counts on a battery of SSM and GEMM microbenchmarks and showing they match.

verification.spec: Run a battery of SSM (varying sequence lengths L in {128,512,2048}, state N in {16,64,128}) and GEMM (various M,K,N) microbenchmarks through both the SystemVerilog RTL (via a simulator like Verilator) and the in-house cycle-accurate Python/C++ simulator. Assert cycle counts match exactly (or within a documented small margin) for each benchmark.

sub_tasks.requirements: A test drives the array through an interleaved sequence of SSM-prefill and GEMM operations (as used in hybrid Mamba–Transformer prefill) by toggling mode bits at runtime, and verifies functional correctness of both phases without reloading operand tiles.

verification.spec: Construct a test sequence that alternates SSM-prefill blocks and GEMM (attention/FFN) blocks as in Nemotron-H hybrid layer patterns, toggling mode bits between them without reloading tiles. Verify final outputs of each stage match reference PyTorch implementations within FP16 tolerance and that no operand-reload stall cycles are inserted purely because of mode switches.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the W-wide vector-unit array with SSM-decode dataflow, dot-product reduction path, SFU row, and unified GEMV mode for the Decode package.
Implement the structural microarchitecture of a single W-wide vector unit and the array of vector units as described in Section 3.3 and Figure 4.
Code has been implemented for a parameterizable vector-unit (VU) module with a configurable SIMD width W (supporting at least W in {8, 16, 32, 64}) that operates on FP16 operands.

verification.spec: Inspect the vector-unit module source. Confirm it is parameterized on SIMD width W and can be instantiated with W in {8,16,32,64}. For each width, instantiate the unit and run a simple lane-parallel multiply on FP16 vectors; verify outputs match numpy FP16 reference.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each vector unit contains exactly three vector registers R1, R2, R3, where R1 and R2 hold input operands and R3 holds intermediate element-wise SSM results as depicted in Figure 4.

verification.spec: Inspect the vector-unit RTL/simulator module and confirm exactly three vector registers named R1, R2, R3 (or equivalent) exist per unit, with R1 and R2 configured as input operand registers and R3 as the intermediate/SSM element-wise result register, matching Figure 4.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each vector unit has a local buffer that can be loaded from external SRAM and provides operands to R1/R2 without going back through the shared SRAM path each cycle.

verification.spec: Inspect and simulate the vector-unit module: verify each vector unit has a local buffer (SRAM/register file) with a load-from-external-SRAM interface. Drive a sequence of R1/R2 reads from the local buffer and confirm they do not incur reads on the external SRAM port each cycle (only on refill), matching Section 3.3.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a vector-unit array module instantiating vector units in a 2D grid whose row count and column count are parameters, with the reference DUET configuration using a 16 x 8 array of 32-wide vector units.

verification.spec: Import the vector-unit array module with parameters rows and cols and confirm they can be set independently. Instantiate with rows=16, cols=8, W=32 (the DUET Decode reference configuration) and confirm 128 vector units are instantiated with 32-wide lanes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a bypass path from external SRAM into the local buffers so that the SSM state cache X_k can be initialized quickly at the start of a decode step, as described in Section 3.3.

verification.spec: Simulate an SSM decode step: initialize state cache X_k in external SRAM, trigger a fast bypass load into the vector-unit local buffers, and verify the load path (a direct SRAM->local-buffer bypass, not through the main compute pipeline) completes within the documented cycle budget and correctly populates local buffers.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the vector-unit datapath supporting element-wise multiply/add, MAC, and dot-product reduction.
Code has been implemented for a lane-parallel W-wide element-wise multiplier stage that computes R1 * R2 element-wise in one cycle.

verification.spec: Load two W-wide FP16 vectors into R1 and R2 of a single vector unit and issue an element-wise multiply. Assert that the result (in R3 or an output port) equals R1*R2 elementwise within FP16 tolerance, and completes in one cycle in the cycle-accurate model.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a W-wide vector add and vector MAC operation using R1, R2, R3 that supports fused multiply-add for expressions of the form R3 <- R1 * R2 + R3.

verification.spec: In a vector-unit testbench, load R1, R2, R3 with known FP16 vectors and issue a fused multiply-add op. Assert R3_new == R1*R2 + R3_old elementwise within FP16 tolerance. Also test the plain vector-add opcode (R3 = R1 + R2).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a tree-based reduction datapath inside each vector unit that reduces a W-wide product vector to a scalar with latency O(log W).

verification.spec: Inspect the vector-unit implementation source. Verify presence of a tree-reduction module (e.g., recursive/log-depth adder tree) that reduces W FP16 products to a scalar. Confirm parameterization by W and that reported latency scales as O(log W) (e.g., W=32 -> 5-stage tree) via code inspection or unit test that measures reduction pipeline depth for W in {8,16,32,64}.

sub_tasks.requirements: The vector-unit reduction datapath has been verified to produce the correct dot-product value for randomized W-wide FP16 input vectors when compared against a reference NumPy/PyTorch dot product, within FP16 numerical tolerance.

verification.spec: Generate randomized FP16 W-wide vectors (W in {8,16,32,64}) and drive them through the vector-unit reduction datapath. Compare the reduced scalar against numpy.dot on the same inputs cast to float16. Assert absolute error <= a documented FP16 tolerance (e.g., 1e-2 relative) across >=1000 trials.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each vector unit exposes both a vector-output mode (returning a W-wide result to R3) and a scalar-output mode (returning the reduced scalar), selectable via a mode/control signal.

verification.spec: Drive a vector unit with the same operands twice, first in vector-output mode (verify a W-wide result appears in R3) and then in scalar-output mode (verify a single scalar equal to the sum-reduction of the elementwise product appears on the scalar output). Confirm the mode is selected via a control/opcode signal.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement column-wise scalar MAC chain combining partial dot products when N > W.
Code has been implemented so that when the SSM state dimension N exceeds the vector width W, N/W vector units in the same column each process a disjoint slice of the state vector.

verification.spec: Configure the vector-unit array with W=32 and issue an SSM decode where N=128 so that N/W=4. Verify that 4 vector units in the same column each receive a disjoint 32-element slice of the state X_k (e.g., by inspecting per-unit operand tags), and that no slice is duplicated across units in the column.
verification.paper_cite: Section 3.3 (SSM-decode dataflow on the vector-unit array)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a scalar MAC chain that runs along each column of the vector-unit array, adding one MAC per vector unit, and that combines the partial scalar dot-product results from vector units within the same column into a single output scalar.

verification.spec: Inspect the vector-unit array module and confirm the existence of a per-column scalar MAC chain wiring: each vector unit in a column contributes one scalar MAC that accumulates into a running scalar propagated down the column, producing one scalar output per column.

sub_tasks.requirements: The column MAC-chain reduction has been verified against a reference implementation: for a state vector of length N distributed across N/W vector units, the summed scalar output equals the full C_k . X_k dot product within FP16 tolerance.

verification.spec: For state dimensions N in {32, 64, 128, 256} with W=32, distribute X_k across N/W vector units in a single column and compute C_k . X_k using the vector unit dot-product path plus the column MAC-chain reduction. Compare the resulting scalar against numpy FP16 dot(C_k, X_k) and assert |diff| <= 1e-2 for all N.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the SFU row and its in-situ integration with the vector-unit array.
Code has been implemented for a single SFU row placed adjacent to the vector-unit array that supports non-linear operations required by Mamba/Transformer decode, including at least exp and SiLU.

verification.spec: Instantiate the SFU row adjacent to the vector-unit array. Drive FP16 inputs through exp and SiLU opcodes and compare against numpy/torch reference for these functions; assert max abs error within the piecewise-approximation tolerance (e.g., < 1e-2 relative).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that SFU outputs feed directly back into vector-unit inputs (registers R1/R2) without requiring a write-back to on-chip SRAM, enabling in-situ consumption of intermediates.

verification.spec: Configure a sequence where a vector unit produces a value, the SFU applies exp/SiLU, and the result feeds directly into R1/R2 of a downstream vector unit. Trace SRAM interface signals and assert no SRAM write occurs for the SFU output during this in-situ dataflow.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the Decode chiplet instantiates 256 SFU units total to match the FlexSFU-based area accounting in Section 4.5.

verification.spec: Inspect the Decode chiplet top-level module or configuration and count instantiated SFU units. Assert the total is exactly 256, matching the FlexSFU-based accounting in Section 4.5.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the SSM-decode dataflow on the vector-unit array (Section 3.3).

Code has been implemented for an SSM-decode controller that, for each token k, sequences the three phases: (i) load X_k into local buffers via the bypass path, (ii) compute A_bar_k * X_k and B_k * u_bar_k and update state, and (iii) compute C_k . X_k via the dot-product reduction path to produce y_k.

verification.spec: Run the SSM-decode controller on a single token k with synthetic A_bar, B, C, u_bar, X inputs. Trace scheduled events and verify the three phases occur in order: (i) X_k load into local buffer (with bypass from external SRAM), (ii) elementwise A_bar_k*X_k and B_k*u_bar_k plus state update, (iii) dot-product C_k . X_k producing y_k. Compare y_k against numpy reference within FP16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the element-wise SSM update X_k = A_bar_k * X_{k-1} + B_k * u_bar_k is computed entirely inside the vector units using R1/R2/R3, with no write-back of A_bar_k * X_{k-1} or B_k * u_bar_k intermediates to shared SRAM.

verification.spec: Instrument the shared-SRAM interface of the vector-unit array during an SSM-decode step. Run a token update and record all SRAM write events. Assert that NO writes correspond to A_bar_k * X_{k-1} or B_k * u_bar_k intermediates — only final X_k (new state) and y_k are permitted to be written back. Verify functional correctness of X_k against numpy reference.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the updated state X_k written back at the end of an SSM decode step matches a reference Mamba SSM reference model that computes X_k = exp(Delta_k * A) * X_{k-1} + (Delta_k * B_k) * u_k within FP16 tolerance.

verification.spec: For a single decode step with randomized FP16 Delta_k, A, B_k, u_k, X_{k-1}, run the vector-unit array SSM-decode dataflow and capture the updated state X_k written back to memory. Compare against a Python reference computing X_k = exp(Delta_k*A)*X_{k-1} + (Delta_k*B_k)*u_k elementwise; assert max abs error < 1e-2 (FP16 tolerance).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the SSM-decode output y_k produced by the vector-unit array equals C_k . X_k + D * u_k (using the same reordering as the Prefill package where applicable) to within FP16 tolerance against a reference PyTorch implementation.

verification.spec: Run a full SSM decode step on the vector-unit array with random FP16 inputs and compute y_k. Compare against a PyTorch reference computing y_k = C_k . X_k + D * u_k (using the (Delta_k * u_k) * B_k reordering where applicable); assert max abs error < 1e-2.

sub_tasks.requirements: The cycle-accurate model reports that the SSM-decode step performs exactly one SSM update per token (matching Section 3.3's statement that decode has one SSM step per token), and that the reduction latency for C_k . X_k scales as O(log N) when N <= W.

verification.spec: Instantiate the vector-unit array decode model and run SSM-decode for a sequence of tokens. Assert that the simulator issues exactly one SSM update per token (count of state-update events == number of tokens). For the C_k . X_k reduction, sweep N in {W, W/2, W/4} (with N <= W) and verify that the measured reduction latency scales as ceil(log2(N)) cycles (allowing +/-1 cycle for pipeline register).

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the unified GEMV mode reusing the same vector-unit datapath.

Code has been implemented for a GEMV mode in which the input vector is loaded once into each vector unit's local buffer while matrix rows are streamed in from external SRAM, matching the description in Section 3.3.

verification.spec: Inspect the vector-unit GEMV implementation. Verify: (a) the input vector is loaded once into each vector-unit local buffer at the start of the op (check trace: exactly one load event per vector unit per GEMV); (b) matrix rows are streamed from external SRAM cycle-by-cycle (check trace: repeated SRAM reads for matrix operands throughout the op).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that GEMV outputs are produced by exactly the same dot-product/reduction path used for C_k . X_k in SSM mode, without requiring any changes to the vector-unit or data-layout hardware.

verification.spec: Inspect the vector-unit array code. Verify that both SSM C_k . X_k computation and GEMV output computation invoke the same dot-product/reduction datapath function/module (e.g., same Python method or same RTL submodule instance) rather than duplicated logic.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that switching between SSM and GEMV modes is controlled via mode bits in the array controller and does not require re-layout of operands in the local buffers or SRAM.

verification.spec: Instantiate the vector-unit array. Perform an SSM-decode op followed by a GEMV op reusing the same operand buffers. Verify: (a) mode is switched by writing a mode-bit register (no reconfiguration API is called that re-lays out buffers); (b) the buffer contents/addressing between the two ops are unchanged (no data movement/copy events are logged between the mode switch).

sub_tasks.requirements: The GEMV mode has been verified against a reference numpy matvec: for random FP16 matrices and vectors of representative decode shapes (e.g., token x FFN weights, query x key cache), the vector-unit array output matches within FP16 tolerance.

verification.spec: For random FP16 matrices/vectors of shapes representative of decode (e.g., 1x4096 * 4096x11008 for FFN; 1x128 * 128xL for query-key), execute the vector-unit array GEMV and compare against numpy fp16 matvec. Assert max abs error <= 1e-2 and relative error <= 1e-2 (FP16 tolerance).

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the memory interface and bandwidth assumptions for the vector-unit array in the Decode package.

Code has been implemented so that the vector-unit array is fed by an on-chip SRAM interface configured for 1024 GB/s bandwidth (matching the Decode-package assumption used in Section 4.2 and Table 3).

verification.spec: Read the Decode-package SRAM interface configuration in the simulator (config file / class attribute). Assert that the SRAM feeding the vector-unit array is set to 1024 GB/s bandwidth.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the local buffer size and refill policy sustain one full W-wide operand read per cycle per vector unit under the modeled SRAM bandwidth, without stalling the multiplier stage for back-to-back GEMV/SSM operations.

verification.spec: Run back-to-back GEMV and SSM operations on the vector-unit array in the cycle-accurate simulator with the modeled 1024 GB/s SRAM. Trace per-cycle multiplier stage activity; assert that the multiplier stage is active (non-stalled) in >=99% of cycles across the steady-state window, indicating the local buffer sustains W-wide operand reads per cycle per vector unit.

sub_tasks.requirements: Verify the configurable behavior of the vector-unit array across widths and array shapes used in the DSE.
Code has been implemented so that the vector-unit array is instantiable and functionally correct at all DSE-relevant configurations: W in {8, 16, 32, 64} and array sizes from 4 x 4 up to 32 x 32.

verification.spec: Programmatically instantiate the vector-unit array for every combination W in {8,16,32,64} x array_size in {4x4, 8x8, 16x8, 16x16, 32x32}. For each configuration, run a small GEMV correctness test against numpy reference and assert output matches within FP16 tolerance. Instantiation must not raise.

sub_tasks.requirements: The cycle-accurate model reproduces the qualitative behavior that with W = 64, vector units are under-utilized on SSM variants whose state dimension N < 64 (utilization drops below 1.0), while W = 32 sustains higher utilization across the SSM kernels considered in Nemotron-H-56B.

verification.spec: Run a Nemotron-H-56B SSM kernel whose state dimension N < 64 (e.g., N=16 or 32) on vector-unit array configs with W=64 and W=32.
